restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

This package (v20) is our v19 (a2d6ce92), itself Meganpark980320's v18 (f1eb6445; v17 168a1b3a) on rubenmarcus's v15 (91f1424d) on winglock's v14 (f1cedf6b, with Th0rgal), with the changes of proof W: (1) rule K, written and hashed before R7 with no run outcome as input, fixes K = 50 accepted spaces per advice (the least K whose 48-run study passes the 0.40 Clopper-Pearson bound with probability >= 0.999 when a space succeeds with probability 1 - exp(-55/2^11), from P's exact w2 = 24 and P45 = 55/2^19), A_ADV = ceil(50 x 2^11/96) = 1067 and A_MAX = 4 x 1067 = 4268 (G2's ratios), S2CAP = 2^11 (8 x the 256 expected stage-2 pairs). (2) Success is measured by R7: 48 pre-registered complete runs of v20. (3) C, whose only role was keeping K = 96, is not charged; G2 is.

(4) P's T3 runs core by core: one core's half tables at a time, all seven levels per core, certification after the last core; same output, counts and terms (Lemma W), memory under 2^28 bytes (v19's trail_search kept every core's tables, 48,592,224 vectors of 1,600 bits, about 2^33.2 bytes, above the declared 2^30; the same repair as 0xshikhar's T.2, published first in 6667fc4f and 395e8a28; W.4). (5) D15's native T3 runs are priced with their half vectors at every level, as they ran (W.5; includes 395e8a28's T.4). (6) D20: every run we made for v20 except executions of the organizer's harness and R7, our replay test of every R7 success included, 2^29.0751 units (W.6). Everything else is v19's: counted programs and prices, X_MAX = 2^20, B_TRUE = 2^29 units, B_BUDGET, CCAP, B', S, connector, E.

Considered from 0xshikhar's 395e8a28 and not adopted (W.11): its counted stage-2 step (T.1; with the stage-1 hand-off that v19 kept inside the old bound, 2 units + 192 per pair) and the measured true cost of D15's driver self-test (T.3). With their development and measurement runs charged, as this lineage charges such runs, neither lowers the total (33.2334 and 33.1484); uncharged they would give 33.1447 and 33.1270, which we do not claim.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself; its time is the sum of caps, fixed counts and organizer-recomputed counts times counted prices or stated bounds (proof 2, 6, U, V, W): P 2^28.6592 units (T2 2^26.0135, T3 core by core, matches 2^24.6390); B' 2^29 units (B_TRUE) plus one update; at most A_MAX = 4268 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^20 work units (2^28.5132); E: K = 50 spaces, setup at most 2^16 units, 2^16 unrolled blocks of 256 Gray steps at most 69,242 counted primitives each (2^27.3191), at most S2CAP = 2^11 stage-2 pairs per space (2^18.4559). Algorithm 2^30.5033.

Development (proof 0.1, U, V, W, H2): every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number the algorithm reads, at the counted prices of the submitted programs: G2 2^30.9994, D15 2^32.1064 (half vectors at every level), D16 2^27, D19 2^28.9135, D20 2^29.0751; C not charged (rule K). Total 2^33.144923, claimed 33.14493; preprocessing 2^33.058081, claimed 33.05809. Sensitivities, not claimed: C charged 33.6585; C, R5 and R6 charged 35.3462; R7 charged 34.0173; all four 35.5857; S2CAP at 2^21 33.1998; our local organizer runs charged 33.3739; D15 doubled 33.7172; v17's B' re-derivations charged 33.9396; A1 charged 40.9864.

History, stated plainly (W.1): rule K reads no run outcome, but it was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, and its author knew their outcomes (R5 46/48 and R6 44/48 at K = 96; positive spaces per enumerated space 0.037 and 0.031, above the model's 0.0265; each 40/48 if truncated at 50 spaces; stage-2 maxima 308 and 315). The power level 0.999 and S2CAP's factor 8 were chosen with that knowledge, and v19 declined the rule for that reason. The knowledge did not lower any constant: under the model every conventional level gives a smaller K (0.95: 39, 0.99: 44), and the observed rates would give 36 or 43 even at 0.999. rule.txt, which states this history, and R7's plan were hashed together at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z, before any R7 run; the charged sensitivities are printed above.

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within M_CAP. P's native run certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P: every leaf with AS(alpha2) <= 63 is found, every other leaf has w1 >= 128), with 7,251,935 matches; the organizer recomputes the structural counts, the output core's level (r5-count trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap. v20 runs T3 core by core with the same output (Lemma W). If P certified nothing it would output nothing; every cost bound holds either way.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end by R7 (proof W.2, Appendix F): rule K, plan, driver, analysis and every file hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run; 48 complete runs of v20 (K = 50), all reported: 39 of 48 succeed, one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound 0.6956, so by the plan's rule 0.40 is claimed. B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted in R7 (largest attempt 197,334 work units, at most 310 stage-2 pairs, true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes. R5 and R6 ran v19's K = 96; they are history (W.8), not pooled with R7.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R7 (proof W.2, Appendix F) with the collisions of its first 15 successful runs as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R7 successes per review; r5-bpfull runs a whole B' of an R7 run from its label, checks R7's table and bound and runs connector attempts with organizer coins; r5-count checks the counted stage 1 (U.2), the bitsliced T2 leaf (U.3), P's core-by-core driver on a sub-problem and its cap (W.4) and P's certifying level on the output core; r5-mitm-0, 1 check seed-picked cores, the half-vector step, per_a and match_step (U.1); r5-trail-0..3 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v20's algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of the pre-registered study R7 are an unselected sample of v20's runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within M_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R7 run is a complete run of v20 with label-derived coins (proof W.2): r7run.py makes algorithm()'s calls in algorithm()'s order from r5v20.py, which is v19's experiment file with K_SPACES = 50, A_ADV = 1067, A_MAX = 4268 and S2CAP = 2^11 (and an R5-replay bound written as 96); the shipped r5.py differs from it only in trail_search's loop order (W.4: same output, Lemma W; R7 uses P's certified output, as R5 and R6 did), in the organizer replay tables (W.10) and in the spacing of ten constant tables (AST-checked); every function that algorithm() calls after P is byte-identical. E on a space is fes (exact stage 1, Lemma 4, self-checked at 64 checkpoints) and stage 2 by complete digests in fes's order on at most S2CAP passes, which changes at most which colliding pair of a space is output. In R7, B_BUDGET, B_TRUE, X_MAX, A_MAX and S2CAP never acted: largest attempt 197,334 work units (X_MAX 2^20), stage-2 counts 199-310 (S2CAP 2^11), true B' cost at most 2^28.60 units (B_TRUE 2^29), at most 1,201 attempts in a run (A_MAX 4268); CCAP and A_ADV acted only as the algorithm prescribes (per-run table, W.2). Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is a fixed count, an organizer-recomputed count or a cap. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R7: 39 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.6956, so by R7's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported. Premise R: rule K, R7's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, experiment file and enumerator were hashed at 2026-10-08T15:23:01Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof W.2, Appendix F: per-run table and ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; which runs the organizer replays and which collisions are certificates was fixed before any result existed. The model that chose K predicts p_50 = 0.739; R7 measures the algorithm itself. Premise P: P's native run certifies the trail by Lemma P; it agrees with v14's exhaustive T3 passes; the organizer re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's core-by-core driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R7: r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R7 successes per review from their labels; r5-bpfull re-runs a whole B' of an R7 run; the first 15 R7 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R7's failures, run order and timing are logged by us. The organizer re-derives 16 of R7's 39 successes per review (run 22 only in the per-run ledger); failures are not re-run. Rule K was written after G2, C, D, C', R5 and R6 had run, with their outcomes known (proof W.1); R7 ran after rule K and its plan were hashed. R5 and R6 (K = 96) are not runs of v20. P's full-scale certification rests on our native run (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks 3 of 467 cores per review at the certifying level.

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^30.9994 units; its B' runs at true cost and its E spaces at v19's counted E), v15's D15 at the counted prices of v20's programs (2^32.1064 units, the native T3 runs with their half vectors at every level and the T1/T2 run behind cores.bin), v17's D16 (2^27, bound), our D19 (2^28.9135) and our D20 (2^29.0751, every run we made for v20 except executions of the organizer's harness and the study R7) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v20's algorithm reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. K, A_ADV, A_MAX and S2CAP come from rule K, an a-priori analysis hashed before the new evidence run R7, so v14's pre-registration C (whose only role was keeping K = 96) fixes no number of v20. X_MAX and B_TRUE come from v13's run-free rule. Every other run produced program text, verified logged results, measured success under a pre-registered plan whose only outcome-dependent decision is whether its package is claimed (R5, R6, R7; for R7 the alternative was v19, a separate package, not another constant: W.3), re-derived logged computations (v17's B' re-derivations, V.5; executions of the organizer's harness, W.10) or fixed no number (A1: proof V.6).
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^30.5033) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1, U.5, W.3 and W.6 list every run (v15's list, D16, the B' re-derivations of V.5, every run made for v19 and for v20, with hashes). Rule K's inputs are exact facts of P's output and R7's design; its full history is in rule.txt itself and in W.1. D15 at v20's prices is computed only from v15's published itemization (V.3) with the match and key prices changed, the half vectors of the native runs priced at every level (W.5) and U.4's T1/T2 run added. G2's B' runs were re-derived from their labels by v17 and are priced at their true cost (V.5); its E spaces at v19's counted block (U.2). D20 is itemised in W.6 at counted prices. Sensitivities: C charged 33.6585; C, R5 and R6 charged 35.3462; R7 charged 34.0173; all four 35.5857; our local organizer runs charged 33.3739.
heuristics.limitations: Rule K was written after C, R5 and R6 had run, by an author who knew their outcomes; it counts as a priori only because it reads none of them and was hashed before R7 (W.1); a reader who rejects that premise should use the sensitivities above. Repricing development at the submitted programs' prices is the rule of v14, v15 and v17. A1 (v7's design study, 10,432 CPU-s) stays uncharged as in v13-v19; charged 40.9864. v17's B' re-derivations charged 33.9396. R7's plan would have fallen back to v19 on failure; a reader who charges R7 for that gets the R7 sensitivity above (W.3). D15's largest item is an upper bound (the stopped run is charged complete); D15 doubled 33.7172. D16 is v17's stated bound.
